entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gerardo Bianchi, known also as Gerardo da Parma or Gerard of Parma, was a pivotal Italian cardinal and papal diplomat whose career unfolded during the tumultuous War of the Sicilian Vespers (1282–1302). Appointed cardinal-priest of Santi XII Apostoli in 1278 by Pope Nicholas III, Bianchi rose through the ranks of the Roman Curia to become a key intermediary in the complex power struggles between the Kingdom of Aragon, the House of Anjou, and the Papacy over control of Sicily and Southern Italy. His strategic appointments as papal legate to various European courts underscore his central role in efforts to broker peace and assert papal suzerainty in a period defined by dynastic rivalries and shifting alliances across the Mediterranean.

Throughout the 1290s, Cardinal Bianchi served as a principal architect of papal foreign policy, dispatched on critical missions to Aragon, France, and Naples. Notably, he was sent by Pope Boniface VIII in 1295 to negotiate the Treaty of Anagni, which aimed to resolve the Sicilian question by compelling James II of Aragon to renounce his claim to Sicily in exchange for Sardinia and Corsica. Though initially accepted, this treaty faced significant resistance from the Sicilian populace and the Aragonese admiral Roger of Lauria, highlighting the limitations of papal diplomacy against popular will and local power structures. Bianchi's efforts also included attempts to reconcile Philip IV of France with Edward I of England, demonstrating the breadth of his diplomatic responsibilities.
